Issue SAK-10208 (Feature Request, Verified, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Group aware Polls
Area: Polls

Polls is a pretty straightforward tool, and it has been without a group-aware feature for years.

Currently, it allows maintain/instructor users to create a new poll for the entire site, and access/student users in the site can answer it. This new feature would not require any new permissions or additional widgets to configure them.

In the creation settings, a simple group selector could display all existing groups in the site. If one or more groups are selected, only access/student users in those groups would be able to answer the poll.

Issue SAK-42033 (Bug, Verified, Fixed, priority Critical)
Title: Calendar import from site with Tests & Quizzes events results in old links
Area: Calendar, Tests & Quizzes (Samigo)

If a user imports from one site to another, calendar events created by Tests & Quizzes remain, with the link to take the test pointing to the original site. 

We have instructors who copy content from a master template into their courses for each semester using the Site Info - Import from Site method. We also have instructors teaching multiple sections who will import from section 1 into section 2. We have seen that if the original site has Tests & Quizzes published and set to create the calendar event, these events are also present in the destination site, with the URL to take the test still pointing to the original. If the instructor publishes the test in the destination site, that test could be on the calendar twice. One link works for students, one does not. 

I feel that these events should not be imported, as they will be recreated if/when the instructor publishes the tests. This would also mirror the behavior of calendar events created by Assignments. 

*Developer Note*: Actually since this fix borrows logic from CC+Import, this fix should suppress the copying of T&Q Dates, Assignment Dates (already in the code), and Discussion Topic deadlines.

Issue SAK-42368 (Bug, Closed, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Site Info > upgrade to Apache FOP 2.0+
Area: Site Info

In SAK-41909 we upgraded the {{xmlgraphics-commons}} library from 1.5 to 2.3. This caused the Site Info > Manage Participants > Printable View to stop working, because site-manage is still using Apache FOP v1.0, which requires a method that's not present in {{xmlgraphics-commons}} v2.0+.

As a stop-gap measure, we added the v1.5 of {{xmlgraphics-commons}} back to the site-manage project so that the feature will work again in the interim (SAK-42346). However, this is only a temporary solution. The proper fix here is to upgrade site-info to Apache FOP v2.0+.

{code:xml}
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.apache.xmlgraphics</groupId>
            <artifactId>fop</artifactId>
            <version>1.0</version>
        </dependency>

        <!-- This old version of xmlgraphics-commons is needed to support Manage Participants > Printable View.
             With the newer (2.3) version (provided by master's pom.xml), you'll get a runtime NoSuchMethodError on org.apache.xmlgraphics.xmp.Metadata.mergeInto(Lorg/apache/xmlgraphics/xmp/Metadata;)V.
             Until the code in SiteInfoToolServlet.generatePDF() is updated to use FOP v2.0+, this needs to stay here. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.apache.xmlgraphics</groupId>
            <artifactId>xmlgraphics-commons</artifactId>
            <version>1.5</version>

Issue SAK-44785 (Feature Request, Resolved, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Convert ckeditor data uri base64 images to Resources linked images
Area: Library, Resources, WYSIWYG Widget (FCK & CK Editor)

https://groups.google.com/a/apereo.org/g/sakai-dev/c/ZR8VEOXMg3c/m/HsITfWsRCAAJ

Is there any way to NOT have ckeditor save pasted in images (or source with base64) as an embedded base64 image?  And instead, automatically add the image to resources and have the ckeditor source link to it?

This plugin looks like it might have some of those features:

https://ckeditor.com/cke4/addon/imagepaste

In our case, we have a class that uses Etudes Meme - Assignments, Tests, Surveys (but I suspect this could happen with Samigo too) and it has 1000s of questions in several question pools.  Many of those questions contain base64 images, which I suspect the instructor pasted into ckeditor.  And I think because of the base64 images, we're seeing some slow queries accessing that tool for that site.

Also, that instructor imports those tests from one semester to the next so the problem continues to happen each semester.  It would be great if we could automatically convert those existing base64 images into an actual file in resources and link to it from the test. (otherwise, we'd have to ask the instructor to manually convert each image into a resources image link)

I also suspect that many sites have pasted in bas64 images into their Overview tool -> Worksite Information.

Further, when I've analyzed Heap Dumps, there are lots of objects in memory that look like base64 images, which I suspect come from the examples above.

Title: LTI Content Item links in the Rich Text Editor should be updated when importing content from another site
Area: LTI

The work on this Jira is documented in this 6 hour long video:  [https://youtu.be/SzgUtgYB_4E|https://youtu.be/SzgUtgYB_4E|smart-link] 

After configuring a content item in LTI for use with the rich text editor, it is possible to embed content any location that the rich text editor is used.

When this content is then imported to a new site the embedded content will not work since the link belongs to the old site. Note that for users that members in the old site as well as the new site then the embedded content will work.

To be fixed - all are both site copy and CC+Archive import:

* Assignments
* Announcements (Site copy only - adding merge() support is another JIRA)

Currently, when processing the SiteStats Event Aggregator job, {{sqlBlockSize}} events are collected starting from a specific {{eventId}}. The next batch then collects another {{sqlBlockSize}} events starting from the previous {{eventId + sqlBlockSize}}.

Issue SAK-52379 (Bug, Closed, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: LTI 1.3 JWKS rotates every 120 minutes because Ignite cache expiry
Area: LTI

*Problem*
  KIDs are changing far too frequently (about every 120 minutes), which is not expected for LMS signing keys.

  *Impact*

* Tool launches intermittently fail when tool-side JWKS cache or KID lookup doesn’t match rapidly changing Sakai keys.
* Seen as “invalid signature / key not found” behavior by vendors.

  *Root Cause*

* Ignite default cache expiry is 120 minutes.
* SakaiKeySetUtil_cache was not configured as eternal, so key material can expire and be regenerated, replacing all KIDs unexpectedly.

  *Expected Behavior*

* Keyset should remain stable and rotate only on intended schedule.
* Rotation should be monthly

  *Proposed Fix*

# Configure org.sakaiproject.basiclti.util.SakaiKeySetUtil_cache as an eternal Ignite cache.

Title: Calendar iCal export should use RRULE for recurring events instead of expanding individual occurrences
Area: Calendar

When exporting the Schedule/Calendar as an iCal feed (.ics), recurring events are expanded into individual VEVENT occurrences instead of being exported with a standard RRULE property. This has been acknowledged in the source code since at least Sakai 2.x with a TBD comment:

BaseCalendarService.java, generateICal():

/* TBD: add to VEvent: recurring schedule, ...
RecurenceRUle x = event.getRecurrenceRule();
*/

h3. Impact

* A class meeting every Monday/Wednesday/Friday for a semester generates ~50 individual VEVENTs instead of a single VEVENT with RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR.
* External calendar clients (Google Calendar, Outlook, Apple Calendar) cannot recognise these events as a recurring series, so users cannot edit or manage the whole series.
* The exported ICS file is unnecessarily large for calendars with many recurring events.
* Sakai-to-Sakai subscriptions (SAK-52617) also benefit: fewer events to process and store on the subscribing side.

h3. Proposed fix

Modify generateICal() in BaseCalendarService to retrieve base (non-expanded) events by calling calendar.getEvents(null, null), then:

* For events with a RecurrenceRule: emit a single VEVENT with an RRULE property built from the rule's frequency, interval, count/until.
* For one-time events: emit as individual VEVENT (current behaviour), filtered to the export time window.

Sakai frequency to RRULE mapping:

* Daily → FREQ=DAILY
* Weekly → FREQ=WEEKLY

Title: Calendar iCal export uses DURATION instead of DTEND causing import failures with many clients
Area: Calendar

The Calendar tool's iCal export method (generateICal in BaseCalendarService) generates events using the DURATION property instead of DTEND. While DURATION is technically valid per RFC 5545, many iCal consumers — including Sakai's own IcalendarReader — do not implement DURATION parsing and silently skip events that lack a DTEND property.

The fix is to replace the DURATION-based VEvent constructor with one that uses explicit DTSTART and DTEND DateTime values, derived from event.getRange().firstTime() and event.getRange().lastTime() respectively, with proper TZID attributes on both properties.

Issue SAK-52900 (Improvement, Resolved, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Polls: bulk CSV import/export should support regional date and delimiter conventions (Excel locale mismatches)
Area: Polls

h2. Problem

Excel on a machine configured with a regional locale that uses a comma as the decimal separator (Spain, most of South America, Portuguese, and most of continental Europe) writes CSV files differently from the US/UK convention the Polls bulk import expected:

* Dates: opening and re-saving a CSV in Excel reformats date cells into the OS's short date convention (e.g. dd/MM/yyyy or dd/MM/yy for Spain) instead of the yyyy-MM-dd the importer required, so a previously valid file could no longer be re-imported after being edited in Excel.
* Delimiter: Excel on those same locales writes CSV files using ';' as the field delimiter instead of ',', because ',' is reserved as the decimal separator - the whole header row was read as a single column and the import was rejected outright.

h2. Solution

When a user pins or unpins a site from the nav bar a burst of sql queries occur to update the order of all sites. This occurs because the order is 0 based and so every sites position must be renumbered.

----

Solution: Switch pinned-site POSITION to a monotonic sort key

Problem
Pinning/unpinning a site forced a full re-sequence of a user's pinned sites. Every addPinnedSite, removePinnedSite, and savePinnedSites call loaded all of a user's PinnedSite rows and rewrote each position to a contiguous 0..N index. This treated position as a dense array index, which:

* loaded and re-saved the entire pinned set on every mutation (extra queries and writes that scale with the number of pinned sites), and
* required reading all rows just to compute "the next position" when appending.

Solution
Treat POSITION purely as a monotonic sort key — values must be strictly increasing for ordering, but may contain gaps and need not be contiguous. Only the relative order matters, not the absolute values.

Issue SAK-52779 (Bug, Closed, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Calendar iCal export uses DURATION instead of DTEND causing import failures with many clients
Area: Calendar

The Calendar tool's iCal export method (generateICal in BaseCalendarService) generates events using the DURATION property instead of DTEND. While DURATION is technically valid per RFC 5545, many iCal consumers — including Sakai's own IcalendarReader — do not implement DURATION parsing and silently skip events that lack a DTEND property.

The fix is to replace the DURATION-based VEvent constructor with one that uses explicit DTSTART and DTEND DateTime values, derived from event.getRange().firstTime() and event.getRange().lastTime() respectively, with proper TZID attributes on both properties.

A centralized grading service for all Sakai tools would simplify and harmonize the overall application. Instead of each tool managing its own grading and then passing grades back to the Gradebook, all tools that generate grades (including Gradebook) would use this new central service. This means that the code for handling grades does not need to be built into each tool separately. The grading service can simply be called by a tool when grading is needed. It also means that faculty can input or update grades from either the Gradebook or the tool (such as Assignments, Samigo, Forums, or Lessons) since the same service is being called in all locations where a grading interface appears.

Issue SAK-49891 (Improvement, Closed, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Tests & Quizzes: Allow question to be copied into the current question pool (duplicate question)
Area: Tests & Quizzes (Samigo)

Currently, if an instructor has a question pool, they can’t create a copy of the question in the current pool. It gives an error - “This question is already in one or more of the specified pools”.

Issue SAK-51826 (Bug, Closed, Fixed, priority Critical)
Title: Reset password doesn't honour the configured site language
Area: Reset Password & Account Validation

Every multi-language organization must offer an internationalized experience for their users. This includes a gateway in every supported language. This is critical in countries with more than one official language, pretty common in Europe.

Reset password tool is internationalized so it loads the user’s preferred language, but this is a very dumb behavior because when somebody is trying to reset his password obviously he is not logged in yet. When there is no user, the tool loads the server’s language.

A mechanism for forcing a language in a site has been present in Sakai for years (see [https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-10393|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-10393|smart-link] ) but Reset Password tool doesn’t honor this setting in Gateway sites.

Issue SAK-51967 (Bug, Closed, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Out-of-order criterion causes rubrics failure for instructor
Area: Rubrics

* In rubrics/impl/src/main/java/org/sakaiproject/rubrics/impl/RubricsServiceImpl.java:385-394, the reorder handler builds sorted with sortedCriterionIds.stream().map(current::get) without checking for missing IDs. When the client sends an ID that no longer exists (stale drag-and-drop data or a concurrent delete), current::get returns null, that null is reinserted into the JPA-managed list, and Hibernate still advances the [user] position for that slot. The next real criterion is written with the following index, leaving a gap such as 1,2,4,5.
** The same pattern appears for ratings in rubrics/impl/src/main/java/org/sakaiproject/rubrics/impl/RubricsServiceImpl.java:397-404, so the symptom can also occur for rbc_rating.order_index.



h2. Fix Ideas

Filter or reject missing IDs before re-adding the list, for example {{sortedCriterionIds.stream().map(current::get).filter(Objects::nonNull)}} (and log/abort if any were missing). Do the equivalent for ratings.

Optionally harden the API by validating that the client sent exactly the current set of IDs, so stale requests fail fast instead of corrupting the ordering.

# Migration from Generic DAO to Spring Repository Pattern

**Date:** 2025-10-06
**Migration Type:** Generic DAO → Spring Repository (SpringCrudRepositoryImpl)

## Overview

This document describes the migration from Sakai's deprecated Generic DAO pattern to Spring's Repository pattern using `SpringCrudRepositoryImpl` located in the Sakai kernel.

## Background

Tools using Generic DAO:
- **Generic DAO Pattern**: `HibernateCompleteGenericDao` with search-based queries
- **Mixed Concerns**: Business logic and data access queries in the DAO class
- **XML Configuration**: Hibernate XML mappings for entities

The migration modernizes this to:
- **Spring Repository Pattern**: `SpringCrudRepositoryImpl` with typed repositories
- **Separation of Concerns**: Service layer for business logic (a class ending in `Service`), repository layer for queries (a class ending in `Repository`)

Issue SAK-52100 (Bug, Closed, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Signup permissions API blocks instructor updates in web component UI
Area: Signup

Summary: Site maintainers using the web component permissions UI for Signup receive a 403 when saving because the Signup service registers its permissions without marking them user-mutable.

Impact: Non-superuser instructors cannot adjust Signup permissions after the REST-based workflow was introduced; the legacy helper masked the issue so it went unnoticed until the web component was adopted.

Reproduction:

# Log in as an instructor (maintain role) and open Signup in a site that uses the SakaiPermissions web component.
# Change any permission toggle and click Save.
# Observe the network response: POST /api/sites/{siteId}/permissions returns 403 Forbidden and the UI shows a generic failure banner.

Root cause: Signup registers its permissions with functionManager.registerFunction(permission) (userMutable = false). The REST controller only allows non-superusers to mutate functions that were registered as user-mutable, so every write attempt is rejected.

Fix: Register all Signup permissions with userMutable = true and improve logging/UI messaging so the 403 surfaces meaningful information.

## Their verdict
- APPROVED

Issue SAK-52434 (Bug, Closed, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Group submission lookup can delete the wrong submission when stale group rosters overlap
Area: Assignments

For group assignments, the submitter list stored on a submission is a persisted snapshot, not a live view of current group membership.

If a student remains on an older group submission’s persisted submitter roster, but their current assignment group resolves to a different group, a later lookup by user id can mis-handle the situation. The group lookup path ends up treating the two group submissions as duplicate user submissions. The repository duplicate-cleanup logic then deletes one submission row during a read/lookup.

  This causes two visible problems:

* the wrong group submission can be returned/displayed
* the valid current group submission can be deleted from {{ASN_SUBMISSION}}

  The delete happens in repository cleanup, so it does not emit the normal {{asn.delete.submission}} event.

Title: Chat Room: more permissions needed for students
Area: Chat

An instructor can give the student role permission to create chat rooms, but that permission alone will not work. The permissions in realms for chat rooms:

* chat.delete.any
* chat.delete.channel
* chat.delete.own
* chat.new
* chat.new.channel
* chat.read
* chat.revise.channel 

By default, students have chat.new and chat.read permissions. If the Create a new chat room permission is set for the student role, it then also gives them the chat.new.channel permission.

With the chat.new.channel permission, the student is unable to save a new chat room. An explanation that when setting the Create a new chat room permission will not work on its own, is really needed for the instructor to understand that more permissions are needed. When the student attempts to save a new chat room, they see the following message:

!image-20260708-153402.png|width=485,alt="image-20260708-153402.png"!

If the student is given the “Set chat room options”, (which equals the chat.revise.channel permission), the student can now modify *any* chat room, including chat rooms created by the instructor.

Two more permissions are really needed for students to be able to create chat rooms and only be able to set options/delete their own chat rooms:

* chat.revise.own.channel  - Set own chat room options
* chat.delete.own.channel - Delete own chat room

!image-20260708-154144.png|width=671,alt="image-20260708-154144.png"!

GradingService is stateful even though it should be stateless. This makes reuse of the same service instance unsafe and fragile.

Issue SAK-51312 (Bug, Verified, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Gradebook modals should trap tab key
Area: Gradebook

Currently, when a modal dialog (e.g., Add Gradebook Item) is opened, keyboard focus is not restricted to the elements within the modal. Users navigating via the keyboard (using {{Tab}} and {{Shift+Tab}}) can inadvertently move focus to interactive elements in the underlying page _behind_ the modal overlay.

*Problem:*

This behavior causes significant issues:

# *Accessibility Barrier (WCAG Failure):* This violates WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 2.4.3 (Focus Order). When a modal dialog is displayed, the keyboard focus order must be logical and confined to the modal's content. Allowing focus to escape disrupts the intended interaction flow, making it difficult or impossible for keyboard-only users and screen reader users to interact effectively with the modal. They can become "lost" on the page behind the overlay.
# *Poor Usability:* Users expect modals to temporarily restrict interaction to the modal's context. Tabbing out of the modal to background elements is confusing and can lead to unintended actions on the main page while the modal is still active.
# *Inconsistent User Experience:* Standard web accessibility patterns dictate that modals should trap focus. Failing to do so creates an inconsistent and non-standard interaction.

*Solution:*

Implemented JavaScript logic within the {{GbModalWindow}} component (or relevant modal component) to:

* Identify all focusable elements within the active modal dialog (including header elements like the close button and content elements).

Issue SAK-52748 (Bug, Closed, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Prevent LTI 1.3 JWKS rotation caused by stale Ignite cache name
Area: LTI

*Short Description*
The fix from [SAK-52379|https://sakaiproject.atlassian.net/browse/SAK-52379], commit {{46ba8af3c01406de87dafbbecc78f3fabd830134}}, configures the pre-SAK-50500 cache name {{org.sakaiproject.basiclti.util.SakaiKeySetUtil_cache}}. Sakai 25 requests {{org.sakaiproject.lti.util.SakaiKeySetUtil_cache}}, so Ignite dynamically creates it with the default 120-minute expiry and the JWKS keys are regenerated.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Deploy Sakai 25 with the SAK-52379 fix.
# Request {{/imsblis/lti13/keyset}} and save the returned keyset and KIDs.
# Keep the Sakai/Ignite cluster running without a restart for more than 120 minutes.
# Request {{/imsblis/lti13/keyset}} again and compare it with the original response.

*Expected Behavior*
The keyset remains stable and rotates only according to {{lti.advantage.key.rotation.days}}, which defaults to 30 days.

*Actual Behavior*
The runtime cache is not matched by the eternal cache declaration. Its entries expire after 120 minutes, causing Sakai to bootstrap replacement public/private keys and change the JWKS KIDs.

*Impact*
LTI 1.3 launches can intermittently fail with invalid-signature or key-not-found errors when tools retain a previously fetched JWKS response.

*Environment*

* App version: Sakai 25.x
* Previous fix: SAK-52379 / {{46ba8af3c01406de87dafbbecc78f3fabd830134}}
* Package rename: SAK-50500

protocol used on the Internet today. Web services, network-enabled
appliances and the growth of network computing continue to expand the

increasing the number of applications that require HTTP support.

Title: Update Apache HttpComponents Client 5.5 GA
Area: Master

The Apache HttpComponents project is pleased to announce 5.5 release of
HttpComponents HttpClient.

This is the first GA release in the 5.5 release series. This release
finalizes the 5.5 APIs and adds several experimental features and
improvements, such as request multiplexing over a shared HTTP/2
connection and the Classic API facade acting as a compatibility bridge
between classic I/O client services and the asynchronous message
transport used internally.

Notable changes and features included in the 5.5 series:

* Improved conformance to RFC 7616 (HTTP Digest Access Authentication).
* The connection pool implementation acts as a caching facade in front
of a standard managed connection pool and shares already leased
connections to multiplex message exchanges over active HTTP/2
connections. This is experimental.
* Extended Auth API and improved authentication protocol logic to
support mutual authentication.
* The Classic API facade now acts as a compatibility bridge between the
classic I/O client services (based on the standard InputStream /
OutputStream model) and the asynchronous message transport used
internally. This is experimental.
* HTTP/2 support for the Fluent Facade (via Classic API facade). This
is experimental.

This maintenance release fixes a regression introduced by the previous release that can cause
a temporary I/O spin during HTTP/2 connection shutdown in case the opposite endpoint fails
to send a GOAWAY frame, and also fixes several bugs related to abnormal termination of HTTP/2
connections found since the last release.

  the underlying I/O session has been fully closed out.

  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Async I/O sessions to explicitly close the I/O channel for output in GRACEFUL
  close mode.
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>

* Bug fix: Classic HTTP server to keep RequestListener thread running when an exception
  occurs during initialization of the incoming connection.
  Contributed by Christian de Waal <christian at de.waal.name>

* Regression: Improved HTTP/2 connection termination in case of the opposite endpoint
  failing to send a GOAWAY frame (correction).
  Contributed by Oleg Kalnichevski <olegk at apache.org>{noformat}

Issue SAK-49670 (Feature Request, Verified, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Roster: Separate user ID from default view
Area: Roster

In Roster tool, the OOB permissions allow only the instructor/maintain role to view all participants. Students by default see only the instructor role. Instructors may want to allow students to view all participants so they can see their peer’s name, profile, picture, and other profile information. The permission to view all participants includes all user’s Sakai profile picture, name, nickname, pronounciation, user ID, and role. Viewing the user’s email address is a separate permission that can be modified for the site. 

In the US, the user ID may not be directory information released by FERPA. There’s very few other locations in Sakai that allows students to see other student’s IDs. (only other one I could find was assignments group submissions) It seems odd that Roster does include the user ID if the default permission is changed to allow students to view their classmates. 

I would like to see viewing the user ID as a separate permission like email. Institutions that consider the User IDs to be directory information can then share them, and those that consider those protected information can allow students to view all participants without sharing the IDs.

Title: SakaiNotifications component fetches notifications on every page load
Area: Web Components

The SakaiNotifications component fetches /api/users/me/notifications on every page load, even if notifications were just fetched seconds ago on a previous page. This creates unnecessary network traffic and server load.

h2. Solution

Implement localStorage caching with 5-minute TTL:

* Check cache before fetching
* Store notifications with timestamp
* Invalidate cache when notifications are cleared/marked as viewed
* Show cache age in console for debugging

Title: Send LTI launch locale as a BCP47 language tag
Area: LTI

*Short Description*
Sakai's LTI 1.3 launch payload emits the {{locale}} claim using Java {{Locale.toString()}}, which produces values like {{en_US}}. LTI Core 1.3 expects {{locale}} to use a BCP47 language tag, such as {{en-US}}.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Configure and launch an LTI 1.3 tool from a Sakai site using a locale with language and region, such as English (United States).
# Inspect the LTI 1.3 launch ID token sent to the tool.
# Check the top-level {{locale}} claim.
# Compare with {{lti/lti-common/src/java/org/sakaiproject/lti/util/SakaiLTIUtil.java}}, where the locale is derived with {{rb.getLocale().toString()}} before being added to the LTI 1.3 launch payload.

*Expected Behavior*
The LTI launch should send the {{locale}} claim as a valid BCP47 language tag, for example {{en-US}}, using Sakai's effective site/user locale.

*Actual Behavior*
The launch can send Java locale-string formatting such as {{en_US}}, which is not the BCP47 format required by LTI Core 1.3.

*Impact*
LTI tools that validate the launch payload against the spec, or that depend on BCP47 locale parsing for localization, may reject the launch or choose the wrong locale. This is an interoperability and conformance issue for LTI 1.3 launches.

*Environment*

Issue SAK-50557 (Bug, Closed, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: LTI: Exceptions thrown for some tools placed on Home site
Area: LTI

For some external tools placed on the tool menu of the Home site, tool launches fail during the redirect phase of the launch. (A concrete example where I’ve encountered this is the Qualtrics LTI 1.3 integration for course evaluations.)

This is because of a distortion that occurs to the login_hint parameter between its encoding in BasicLTISecurityServiceImpl.redirectOIDC and decoding in OIDCServlet.handleOIDCAuthorization.

For example, a URI referring to content on a Home (user) site like the following:

{{/access/lti/site/~e9376efc-2102-4eb8-ac60-0e7ba383cb50/content:118}}

Will be base64 encoded to:

{{L2FjY2Vzcy9sdGkvc2l0ZS9+ZTkzNzZlZmMtMjEwMi00ZWI4LWFjNjAtMGU3YmEzODNjYjUwL2NvbnRlbnQ6MTE4}}

This string is then posted as the login_hint parameter. However, when received by OIDCServlet.handleOIDCAuthorization, the following string is:

{{L2FjY2Vzcy9sdGkvc2l0ZS9 ZTkzNzZlZmMtMjEwMi00ZWI4LWFjNjAtMGU3YmEzODNjYjUwL2NvbnRlbnQ6MTE4}}

It’s the same string, except that the ‘+’ in the original string is supplanted with a space ‘ ‘. Therefore, the base64 decoding of the now distorted string results in unexpected characters. And the subsequent attempt to redirect fails. (An exception is thrown.)

I’ve attached a screencast to demonstrate the problem and a proposed fix.

Title: LTI Remove unused lti13_setting field from tool and content and lti13 flag from content
Area: LTI

The {{lti13_settings}}field is actually a hold over from LTI 2.0 - and I left it in for a while hoping that LTI 1.3 would re-add a settings service (which I felt was a good feature).  But time passed, and the feature was not added to LTI 1.3 - it was superseded by the much more complex link service so it is not likely to come back.  We removed the support for the (never used) settings service to set and get the settings some time ago and it is time to remove the columns from the database and model as well.

Also there is an {{lti13}} flag in content that needs to be removed.  The {{lti13}} flag in the tool is what is used.  Back in the day, I thought as part of the LTI 1.1 → 1.3 transition it might be nice to back to have one content item use 1.1 while all the rest used 1.3.  The LTI 1.1 to 1.3 transition across all LMS’s was weird and spotty and few LTI tools really were prepared from a content item level flexibility of launch type.  The {{lti13}} flag in _content_ is not read or written anywhere in the code base so it should be removed.  

The {{lti13}} flag in the tool is essential and will remain the signal to launch code as to which protocol to use.

Issue SAK-52379 (Bug, Closed, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: LTI 1.3 JWKS rotates every 120 minutes because Ignite cache expiry
Area: LTI

*Problem*
  KIDs are changing far too frequently (about every 120 minutes), which is not expected for LMS signing keys.

  *Impact*

* Tool launches intermittently fail when tool-side JWKS cache or KID lookup doesn’t match rapidly changing Sakai keys.
* Seen as “invalid signature / key not found” behavior by vendors.

  *Root Cause*

* Ignite default cache expiry is 120 minutes.
* SakaiKeySetUtil_cache was not configured as eternal, so key material can expire and be regenerated, replacing all KIDs unexpectedly.

  *Expected Behavior*

* Keyset should remain stable and rotate only on intended schedule.
* Rotation should be monthly

  *Proposed Fix*

# Configure org.sakaiproject.basiclti.util.SakaiKeySetUtil_cache as an eternal Ignite cache.

Sakai treats `activityProgress` as a state machine for assignment submission status:

   - Sakai defaults missing `activityProgress` to completed/submitted behavior
   - This is intentional compatibility behavior for grade pushes without lifecycle state

Sakai Support for LTI Deployments
=================================

IMS LTI 1.3 includes a concept called `deployment_id` for servers that serve multiple tenants
from the same URL, or for SaaS-style hosts that use a single platform signing key pair
for JWTs across all hosted instances (for example Canvas or Blackboard). In Sakai we use
one key pair per server. We still need to support multiple tenants for LTI tools—law,
engineering, or even a single site when a tool wants different billing for different areas
of the university.

Most tools sell to the "whole university" and in effect ignore the `deployment_id` from Sakai
for authorization decisions. The tools must still receive the `deployment_id` and send it
on certain API calls; in those situations the tool typically accepts whatever value the LMS
sends and echoes it as required.

Treat `deployment_id` values as alphanumeric slugs: ASCII letters, ASCII digits, hyphens, and underscores. If Sakai
sees other characters, it removes them at launch time so the protocol does not fail. For
example, `"Hello 🌴 123"` becomes `"Hello123"` because the emoji and spaces are not allowed.

Issue SAK-52678 (Bug, Resolved, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Send LTI launch locale as a BCP47 language tag
Area: LTI

*Short Description*
Sakai's LTI 1.3 launch payload emits the {{locale}} claim using Java {{Locale.toString()}}, which produces values like {{en_US}}. LTI Core 1.3 expects {{locale}} to use a BCP47 language tag, such as {{en-US}}.

*Steps to Reproduce*

# Configure and launch an LTI 1.3 tool from a Sakai site using a locale with language and region, such as English (United States).
# Inspect the LTI 1.3 launch ID token sent to the tool.
# Check the top-level {{locale}} claim.
# Compare with {{lti/lti-common/src/java/org/sakaiproject/lti/util/SakaiLTIUtil.java}}, where the locale is derived with {{rb.getLocale().toString()}} before being added to the LTI 1.3 launch payload.

*Expected Behavior*
The LTI launch should send the {{locale}} claim as a valid BCP47 language tag, for example {{en-US}}, using Sakai's effective site/user locale.

*Actual Behavior*
The launch can send Java locale-string formatting such as {{en_US}}, which is not the BCP47 format required by LTI Core 1.3.

*Impact*
LTI tools that validate the launch payload against the spec, or that depend on BCP47 locale parsing for localization, may reject the launch or choose the wrong locale. This is an interoperability and conformance issue for LTI 1.3 launches.

*Environment*

* App version: Sakai trunk / LTI 1.3 launch implementation

## The task
Issue SAK-52779 (Bug, Closed, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Calendar iCal export uses DURATION instead of DTEND causing import failures with many clients
Area: Calendar

The Calendar tool's iCal export method (generateICal in BaseCalendarService) generates events using the DURATION property instead of DTEND. While DURATION is technically valid per RFC 5545, many iCal consumers — including Sakai's own IcalendarReader — do not implement DURATION parsing and silently skip events that lack a DTEND property.

The fix is to replace the DURATION-based VEvent constructor with one that uses explicit DTSTART and DTEND DateTime values, derived from event.getRange().firstTime() and event.getRange().lastTime() respectively, with proper TZID attributes on both properties.

## The task
Issue SAK-52715 (Bug, Closed, Fixed, priority Major)
Title: Skin: unchecked Bootstrap check inputs render white in dark mode
Area: Library

h2. Symptom

In dark mode, unchecked checkboxes/radios that use Bootstrap's {{.form-check-input}} class render with a white background — e.g. the Lessons checklist boxes glare white on a dark page.

h2. Root cause

The skin ({{library/.../sass/base/_defaults.scss}}) themes the _checked_ and _disabled_ states of checkboxes/radios but never sets an _unchecked_ background, so Bootstrap's {{--bs-form-check-bg}} (white) shows through on {{.form-check-input}} elements.

h2. Fix

Set the unchecked background to transparent on the shared checkbox/radio rule so it matches plain inputs. Light theme is unaffected.

*Problem:* The Lessons inline Question Text editor starts with a collapsed toolbar, so its collapse/expand control is prominent. In dark mode that control renders with a white background, and once the toolbar is expanded its arrow disappears (dark #333 arrow on the dark toolbar).
